themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 131 THIS WEEK—a 248% spike vs. the 37.6 weekly average—signaling rapid deterioration across CD 405, likely driven by winter weather or deferred maintenance hitting critical mass.
evidence: 131 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 37.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.09)
248% spike represents sharp acceleration from baseline
Consistent with winter conditions but timing and magnitude suggest systemic issue requiring immediate response
reporting_angles: Map hotspots of complaints across Ridgewood/Glendale/Middle Village to identify which streets are worst-hit and why
Interview DOT on repair timeline and resource allocation; ask whether this week's spike is weather-reactive or reflects years of deferred maintenance flagged in CB budget requests

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK—a 367% spike vs. the 1.5 weekly average—suggesting potential health code violations or inspectional gaps in local restaurants and food vendors.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.5)
367% spike indicates concentrated problem in short timeframe
Complaints likely tied to specific violations (temperature, sanitation, pests) affecting multiple locations
reporting_angles: Obtain DOHMH inspection records for the 7 complaints filed this week; identify common violation patterns and which establishments/cuisines are affected
Interview Health Department on whether this reflects inspector capacity issues or a genuine surge in violations; cross-reference with any prior complaints at repeat offenders

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Non-Emergency Police Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped 162% to 17 LAST WEEK (vs. 6.5 weekly average) and non-emergency police matters surged 159% to 23 LAST WEEK (vs. 8.9 average), suggesting growing street-use conflicts or quality-of-life issues outpacing enforcement capacity.
evidence: Obstruction complaints: 17 LAST WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.42, 162% spike)
Non-emergency police matters: 23 LAST WEEK vs. 8.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.19, 159% spike)
Parallel rise suggests coordinated neighborhood disturbance rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Analyze which types of obstructions (debris, vehicles, vendors, sidewalk use) are driving complaints; map geographic clustering
Interview NYPD and local precinct on staffing, response times, and whether they're seeing coordinated disorder or fragmented complaints; ask about repeat addresses

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Infrastructure Strain
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints, dumpster complaints, and litter basket requests collectively jumped 700–833% LAST WEEK, signaling either a sanitation service breakdown or acute accumulation of refuse (possibly weather/holiday-related) that residents expect city to address.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 7 LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.74, 833% spike)
Dumpster complaints: 7 LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 9.45, 833% spike)
Litter basket requests: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, 700% spike)
Three-vector surge suggests system-wide sanitation backlog rather than isolated complaint
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine whether last week included missed collections, holiday disruptions, or equipment failures; ask for service level data by sanitation district
Document resident experience: are sidewalks visibly dirtier, are dumpsters overflowing, are street sweepers absent? Get photos and quotes from residents and local business owners

themes_detail.label: Residential Disorder & Building Conditions
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile and obstruction complaints (3100% and 162% spikes, respectively) combined with 379 building permit filings (291 alterations) suggest active construction activity creating debris/obstruction while community board repeatedly requests building inspector staffing—a structural capacity gap.
evidence: Wood pile complaints: 4 three weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, 3100% spike)
379 DOB filings in last 90 days (291 alterations) suggest sustained construction pressure in district
Community Board budget requests include 'assign additional building inspectors'—repeated ask suggests chronic understaffing
reporting_angles: Cross-reference wood pile and obstruction complaint locations with DOB permit maps; identify which construction projects are generating complaints and whether they hold proper debris licenses
Interview DOB on inspector staffing levels, complaint resolution timelines, and whether CD 405 is understaffed relative to permit volume; ask CB why this request recurs annually
